definition_en: a stretched state, or a feeling of worry and strain between people
core_image: 一根被拉到极限、随时会断的绳
scene: 谈判桌上谁都不说话。The rope was stretched until the tension could be felt.
sceneCN: 这里 tension 是「拉力、张力」（第 1 个义项：被拉伸的状态）；句意：绳子被拉紧到能感觉到张力。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根 tens- 构成，义为「绷紧的」
tense 加副词后缀，义为「紧张地」
tension 加否定后缀，义为「无张力的」

senses.title: A stretched state
senses.definition: the state of being stretched tight
senses.definitionCN: 被拉紧的状态
senses.example: The tension in the rope held the bridge steady.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子的张力让桥保持稳定。
senses.why: The Latin root tendere means to stretch, so a stretched thing carries force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 tendere 意为「拉伸」，被拉伸的东西就带着力。

senses.title: A feeling of strain
senses.definition: a nervous, worried feeling
senses.definitionCN: 紧张、不安的情绪
senses.example: She felt the tension rise before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前她感到紧张加剧。
senses.why: A mind stretched by worry works like a rope stretched by force.
senses.whyCN: 被焦虑「拉伸」的心，就像被外力拉紧的绳。

senses.title: Strained relations
senses.definition: a situation where people or countries distrust each other
senses.definitionCN: 人与人或国与国之间互不信任的局势
senses.example: Trade talks reduced the tension between the two nations.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易会谈缓解了两国间的紧张。
senses.why: Distrust pulls people apart the way force pulls a rope.
senses.whyCN: 不信任把人拉开，正如外力把绳拉开。

intro.en: Tension comes from Latin tendere, to stretch.

items.cn: 词义扩展到心理与社会的紧张。

note.en: Tension is compared with look-alike words and with words for strain.
note.cn: 把 tension 与形近词及表示紧张的词作对比。

definition_en: a portable shelter made of cloth held up by poles
core_image: 几根杆子撑起的一块防布
scene: 山谷里过夜的营地。We pitched the tent beside the lake.

senses.title: A portable shelter
senses.definition: a shelter of cloth supported by poles and ropes
senses.definitionCN: 用杆子和绳子撑起布料做成的可移动住所
senses.example: We pitched the tent beside the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把帐篷搭在湖边。
senses.why: The word came from Latin tendere, to stretch — the cloth is stretched on poles.

normalIntro.cn: tent 是拉伸撑在杆上、在户外撑起一个家的布。

The tent pegs came loose in the wind.
They slept in a small tent all week.

normal.en: Take down the tent before the rain.
A big tent held the whole family.
normal.cn: 一顶大帐篷装下了全家。

abstract.cn: 拉伸的布变成了一个房间。

abstract.en: Four poles and some rope draw a shelter in the air.
abstract.cn: 四根杆加些绳，在空中画出住所。

abstract.en: A tent is a home you can fold.

definition_en: a word with a special meaning, a school period, or a condition of an agreement
core_image: 一块界碑，圈定一个意义的范围
scene: 法官宣读协议的最后一部分。The two sides agreed to the terms.
sceneCN: 这里 term 是「条款」（第 3 个义项）；句意：双方同意了这些条款。

术语学；一组术语

senses.title: A special word
senses.definition: a word or expression with a precise meaning in a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域有确切含义的词或表达
senses.example: Photosynthesis is a term from plant science.
senses.exampleCN: 光合作用是植物科学的术语。
senses.why: A term is a boundary marker that fixes where a meaning ends.
senses.whyCN: 术语是划界的标记，把一个意义的范围固定下来。

senses.title: A fixed period
senses.definition: a fixed period of time, such as a school session or an office
senses.definitionCN: 固定的一段时间，如学期或任期
senses.example: The new term begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 新学期九月开始。
senses.why: A set period is the time boundary drawn around an activity.
senses.whyCN: 固定期限是为活动画出的时间边界。

senses.title: A condition of agreement
senses.definition: a condition stated in an agreement, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 协议中写明的条件，常用复数
senses.example: The two sides agreed to the terms.
senses.exampleCN: 双方同意了这些条款。
senses.why: Each clause is a boundary line both sides must stay within.
senses.whyCN: 每一条款都是双方必须遵守的边界线。

senses.title: To name something
senses.definition: to give something a particular name or description
senses.definitionCN: 给某物一个特定的称呼或说法
senses.example: Critics termed the play a landmark.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称这部戏为一座里程碑。
senses.why: Naming fixes a thing inside the boundary of a chosen word.
senses.whyCN: 命名就是把事物圈进所选词语的边界之内。

senses.title: A relation or standing
senses.definition: the way two people or groups regard each other, as in on good terms
senses.definitionCN: 人与人或群体之间彼此的看法，如「关系好」
senses.example: They are on friendly terms again.
senses.exampleCN: 他们重新和好如初。
senses.why: A relationship is measured by the standing each side keeps within shared lines.
senses.whyCN: 关系由双方共同边界内各自所处的位置衡量。

definition_en: very bad, causing fear, or extreme in degree
core_image: 让人后背发凉的一团阴影
scene: 门后传来奇怪的声音。The noise outside was terrible.
sceneCN: 这里 terrible 是「可怕的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：外面的声音很可怕。

derivatives.zh: terrible 加副词后缀，义为「非常；可怕地」
terrible 加名词后缀，义为「可怕」

senses.title: Causing fear
senses.definition: making people feel very frightened
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到极度恐惧的
senses.example: The noise outside was terrible.
senses.exampleCN: 外面的声音很可怕。
senses.why: The root terrere means to frighten, so the base sense is fear itself.
senses.whyCN: 词根 terrere 意为「使惊恐」，本义就是恐惧。

senses.title: Very bad
senses.definition: of very poor quality or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 质量极差或令人不快的
senses.example: The traffic was terrible this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今天早上交通糟透了。
senses.why: Something frightening becomes something we dread facing, hence bad.
senses.whyCN: 令人恐惧的事变成了我们不愿面对的事，进而引申为糟糕。

senses.title: Extreme in degree
senses.definition: very great in amount or force
senses.definitionCN: 数量或强度上极大
senses.example: He felt a terrible weight on his chest.
senses.exampleCN: 他感到胸口压着千斤重担。
senses.why: Fear magnifies what it touches, so the word scales up size and force.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧会放大所触及之物，因此词义可表程度巨大。

definition_en: used to compare two things or to mark what follows
